content.text:
I didn't free any space. When I tried to run the cleanup, every call was rejected with "tool call limit reached; not run", so nothing in the lakehouse has changed.

**What I found:** there are 7 tables, and all their snapshots are appends, with no branches or tags.
- **`db.orders`**: 8 snapshots, the oldest from 2026-07-07. This is the most history of any table.
- **`db.events`**: 6 snapshots, going back to 2026-07-27.
- **`db.customers`**: 3 snapshots. **`db.customers_pii`**, **`db.orders_staging`** and **`prod.orders`**: 2–3 snapshots each.
- **`prod.customers`**: 1 snapshot, so there's nothing to reclaim.

**What I tried to do:** a low-risk cleanup of the development (`db`) tables only. I wanted to expire snapshots older than 2026-10-05 (30 days ago) while always keeping the newest 2 per table. That would have removed 4 old snapshots from `db.orders` and 4 from `db.events`, and left the other tables as they are. After that, I planned to delete orphan files older than a week. I didn't intend to delete any table data or touch production. Expiring snapshots does mean you can no longer roll back to those versions.

**Next steps:** in a new session, the cleanup above can be run as described. If you want to include production as well, expiring `prod.orders` snapshot 100022 (from 2026-07-27) would free a bit more. I'd want your confirmation before touching anything in production.
